payload.rationale: EIA weekly gasoline price data for the first half of September 2026 shows a notable increase from the August average (from ~$4.19 to ~$4.37-$4.45). Historically, the seasonal adjustment factor for gasoline in September is highly positive, adding roughly 2 percentage points to the non-seasonally adjusted change. This suggests the seasonally adjusted gasoline index could rise by 5% to 7% in September. Given gasoline's relative importance of ~3.77%, this component alone could contribute 0.2% to 0.25% to the headline CPI. Assuming core CPI and food components increase at their recent trend of 0.1% to 0.3%, the unrounded headline CPI is highly likely to be around 0.3% to 0.5%. Therefore, the probability that the rounded 1-decimal CPI-U will strictly exceed 0.2% (i.e., be 0.3% or higher) is quite high.
limitations: Gasoline prices for the second half of September are unknown and could drop sharply.
Core CPI and food components could unexpectedly decelerate.
EIA weekly retail prices are an approximation of the BLS gasoline index methodology, which includes different sampling and weighting.
Seasonal factors are subject to revision and might differ from historical patterns.
